_source: Transcribed from the Kaggle log of notebook 06-small-object-2d-feasibility, version 1 (CPU, 105.5 s, 2026-11-14). Pictures here are screenshots of the notebook figures; the full-resolution PNGs, instances.csv and summary.json are in that version's Output tab.
visual_check: Close-ups: switches (yellow frame / dark square in intensity), smoke detectors (round, ceiling), exit signs and fire extinguishers clearly recognisable; outlets clearly recognisable (socket face) when scanned at 2-3 mm, poorly when at 6 mm or very oblique (S168 #1, S178 #1). Panoramas from the tripod position look like photographs; all S163 objects recognisable by eye; S169 outlets are a row of sockets on wall trunking behind a desk, visible but small (22-220 px).
decision: GO for the 2D route (zero-shot first). Caveats: very few objects per class (train: Damper 2, Exit sign 7, Fire terminal 14, Outlet 7, Switch 4; val: 1/1/1/4/1) -> no 2D training from our data alone; validation IoU of four classes rests on a single object.
